result.summary: Updates fee estimation to fall back to the block policy estimator when the mempool estimator cannot produce an estimate, and clears mempool estimator statistics if mempool loading fails during startup. It also renames the default fee estimator RPC option in estimatesmartfee from "none" to "auto" while keeping backwards compatibility.
result.problem: When the mempool fee estimator does not yet have enough data, fee estimation requests can fail with an error instead of using available block policy estimates. Additionally, if mempool loading fails or persistence is disabled on restart, leftover mempool fee tracking data can cause distorted fee estimates, such as returning the minimum fee rate floor.
evidence: PR description: "Falls back to the `block_policy` fee rate estimator when `mempool_policy` is not available. This preserves the previous behavior and lets users who update their node keep using `block_policy` estimates until the mempool policy has finished gathering stats and is ready to serve estimates."

Commit 305f7df895: "When the mempool fails to load at startup (persistence disabled, or a missing or corrupt mempool.dat), init notifies the fee_rate_estimator_man, which clears its tracked mined-block window. Otherwise the estimator would keep a window describing a mempool the node no longer has and, once the mempool refilled, serve an estimate built on it."
result.card: This PR updates estimatesmartfee to fall back to the block policy fee estimator when the mempool estimator lacks sufficient data, and clears mempool tracking stats when mempool.dat fails to load at startup. It also renames the default estimator parameter from "none" to "auto". Without this fallback, updating nodes can fail to serve fee estimates during mempool stats gathering, and restarts with lost mempools risk serving estimates based on stale data. The PR is targeted for backport to 32.x and unblocks the remainder of #36182.
uncertainties: Full diff was not provided, though commit messages and PR description detail the exact changes.

risk.why: Flaws in fee rate estimator fallback logic or state resets could cause RPC clients to receive inaccurate fee rates, leading to overpayment or stuck transactions.
